parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A coil of insulated wire is wound on a copper core, as illustrated in Fig. 10.1.
An alternating current is passed through the coil.
The heating effect of the current in the coil is negligible.
Explain why the temperature of the core rises.

markscheme_points.text: (non-uniform) magnetic flux in core is changing
induces (different) e.m.f. in (different parts of) the core

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in ideal gas laws and thermodynamics that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
Hint 4: Clearly show every intermediate algebraic substitution and ensure your final value has correct physical units.
parts.proper_answer: (non-uniform) magnetic flux in core is changing; induces (different) e.m.f. in (different parts of) the core; (eddy) currents form in the core; which give rise to heating

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Two hollow tubes of equal length hang vertically as shown in Fig. 10.2.
One tube is made of plastic and the other of aluminium.
Two small similar bar magnets A and B are held above the tubes and then released simultaneously.
The magnets do not touch the sides of the tubes.
Explain why magnet B takes much longer than magnet A to fall through the tube.

markscheme_points.text: as magnet falls, tube cuts magnetic flux
with energy taken from falling magnet
or (eddy) currents produce magnetic field (M1) that opposes motion of magnet (A1) so magnet B has acceleration < g or magnet B has smaller acceleration/reaches terminal speed

hints: Hint 1: Consider what happens to the magnetic flux linked with the aluminium tube as the magnet falls through it.
Hint 2: Apply Faraday's law to explain why an electromotive force and resulting eddy currents are induced in the aluminium tube.
Hint 3: Apply Lenz's law to explain how the magnetic field of the eddy currents produces an upward opposing force on the magnet.
Hint 4: Explain the energy transfers: gravitational potential energy is converted to kinetic energy and thermal energy in the tube via eddy current heating.
Hint 5: Conclude why the magnet in the aluminium tube accelerates at less than $g$ and reaches a terminal speed, unlike in the plastic tube.
parts.proper_answer: as magnet falls, tube cuts magnetic flux; e.m.f./(eddy) currents induced in metal/aluminium (tube); (eddy) current heating of tube; with energy taken from falling magnet; or (eddy) currents produce magnetic field (M1) that opposes motion of magnet (A1) so magnet B has acceleration < g or magnet B has smaller acceleration/reaches terminal speed
